name: Italian Chicken with Peppers
pitch: Your chicken, bell peppers, and onion are basically the heart of this rustic Italian braise — you just need a can of tomatoes to pull it all together.
steps: Heat a glug of oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season your chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then brown them on all sides — about 3-4 minutes per side. Set aside on a plate.
In the same pan, add your sliced onion and bell pepper. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. Toss in a couple of minced garlic cloves if you have them (totally optional but great).
Add a splash of red wine vinegar (or a small squeeze of lemon juice works too) and scrape up any brown bits from the bottom — that's flavor.
Pour in a can of diced tomatoes, add a pinch of dried basil or Italian seasoning, and a pinch of red pepper flakes if you like a little heat. Nestle the chicken back in.
Cover and simmer on medium-low for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Taste, adjust salt, and serve as-is or over rice or pasta.

name: Easy Baked Chicken with Peppers and Onion
pitch: This is simple, hands-off comfort food — just season your chicken, tuck it in with peppers and onion, and let the oven do the work.
steps: Heat your oven to 400°F (higher than the original — it'll give you better color in less time). Pat your chicken dry with a paper towel and place it in a 9x13 baking dish.
Slice your bell pepper and onion into chunky pieces and scatter them around the chicken in the dish.

Drizzle everything with oil. Season generously with salt, pepper, and paprika if you have it — smoked paprika is great here. A pinch of dried rosemary or thyme works too, but honestly just salt and paprika is enough.
No chicken broth? No problem — just add a small splash of water to the bottom of the dish to keep things from drying out. If you have half a lemon, squeeze it over the top.
Roast uncovered for 40-50 minutes until the chicken is golden and cooked through (internal temp 165°F, or juices run clear). Let it rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken and Veggie Rice Skillet
pitch: This is less of a traditional risotto and more of a hearty one-pan rice dish — but with your chicken, peppers, and onion, it's a solid weeknight meal if you've got rice and a few extras.
steps: Cut your chicken into bite-sized pieces and cook them in a large pan with a little oil over medium-high heat until golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, add your diced onion and bell pepper and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add garlic if you have it.
Add your rice (about 1 cup) and stir it around in the pan for a minute to toast it slightly.

Pour in about 2 cups of chicken broth — or just use water with a good pinch of salt if you don't have broth. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on low for about 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir the chicken back in. If you have any cheese — parmesan, cheddar, whatever — sprinkle some on top. Taste for salt and serve straight from the pan.
